from: Datum Atlas 45de29b (MIT); each value names its source

atlas-typ.title: Datum Atlas compilation of typical property ranges for generic materials
atlas-typ.note: Our own compilation of typical ranges for generic grades, written from general engineering handbooks and textbooks. Draft: each value is still to be referenced to a specific table, standard or datasheet.

mil5j.title: MIL-HDBK-5J: Metallic Materials and Elements for Aerospace Vehicle Structures
mil5j.note: Design allowables for aerospace alloys (superseded by the MMPDS series). Values here are typical ranges around the handbook data, not design allowables.

cmh17.title: MIL-HDBK-17: Composite Materials Handbook, Volumes 2 and 3 (Polymer Matrix Composites)
cmh17.note: Properties and design guidance for fibre composites (continued as CMH-17). Values here are typical ranges for generic laminates.

fpl-wood.title: Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (General Technical Report FPL-GTR-282)

nist-srd30.title: NIST Structural Ceramics Database (Standard Reference Data 30)
nist-srd30.note: Properties of advanced structural ceramics from the literature.

npl-tables.title: Tables of Physical and Chemical Constants (online edition)
npl-tables.note: Thermal and physical properties of the elements and common materials.

ds-sij-6582.title: Steel 1.6582 (34CrNiMo6, AISI 4337/4340) datasheet
ds-sij-6582.note: Quenched and tempered, by section size; the European equivalent of 4340.

ds-acm-17-4.title: 17-4PH Stainless Steel Bar (AMS 5643 / AMS 5622) technical data sheet

ds-jt-c70600.title: C70600 copper
ds-jt-c70600.note: Producer's product page; soft to hard temper.

ds-combmet-430.title: 430 stainless steel alloy datasheet
ds-combmet-430.note: Annealed strip and sheet (ASTM A240 minimums); physical properties.

materials.name: Alumina (99.5 % Al₂O₃)
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Silicon carbide (sintered)
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Silicon nitride (sintered)
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Zirconia (yttria-stabilised, Y-TZP)
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Boron carbide
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more. Oxidises in air above about 600 °C.

materials.name: Cemented carbide (WC, 6 % Co)
materials.notes: Strength is the transverse rupture strength. Scrap is recycled.

materials.name: Aluminium nitride
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Soda-lime glass
materials.notes: Annealed. Design strength depends on surface flaws.

materials.name: Borosilicate glass
materials.notes: Low expansion, good thermal shock resistance.

materials.name: Porcelain (electrical, alumina-silicate)
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength (modulus of rupture); tensile strength is lower and varies more.

materials.name: Concrete (normal weight)
materials.notes: Plain, not reinforced. Crushed for aggregate rather than recycled.

materials.name: Sapphire (single-crystal alumina)
materials.notes: Properties depend on the direction in the crystal.

materials.name: Silicon carbide, reaction bonded
materials.notes: Contains free silicon, so it stays below about 1380 °C.

materials.name: Hexagonal boron nitride, hot pressed
materials.notes: Machinable; properties depend on the pressing direction. Oxidises above about 900 °C in air.

materials.name: Graphite, fine-grained isostatic
materials.notes: Oxidises in air above about 450 °C; in vacuum or inert gas it works above 2500 °C.

materials.name: Lithium aluminosilicate glass-ceramic
materials.notes: Expands almost nothing: about 0 ± 0.1 µstrain/°C between 0 and 50 °C (left out of the expansion axis, which is logarithmic).

materials.name: Aluminosilicate glass, chemically strengthened
materials.notes: Strength is the flexural strength after ion exchange; it falls when the surface is scratched.

materials.name: Sandstone
materials.notes: Very variable; strength falls when wet.

materials.name: Gypsum plaster
materials.notes: Loses its water of crystallisation above about 45 °C; this makes it a good fire barrier.

materials.name: CFRP, quasi-isotropic laminate (carbon/epoxy)
materials.notes: About 60 % fibre by volume; in-plane properties.

materials.name: CFRP, unidirectional (carbon/epoxy), along the fibres
materials.notes: About 60 % fibre by volume, loaded along the fibres.

materials.name: CFRP, woven carbon fabric/epoxy
materials.notes: About 55 % fibre by volume, along the warp.

materials.name: CFRP, high-modulus unidirectional
materials.notes: About 60 % fibre by volume, loaded along the fibres.

materials.name: GFRP, chopped strand mat/polyester
materials.notes: About 30 % glass by weight; the same in every direction in the plane.

materials.name: Flax fibre/epoxy, unidirectional
materials.notes: About 40 % fibre by volume; damps vibration well.

materials.name: Carbon fibre/PEEK, unidirectional
materials.notes: About 60 % fibre by volume; can be re-melted, welded and recycled. Along the fibres it expands about 0 to 2 µstrain/°C (left out of the expansion axis, which is logarithmic).

materials.name: Carbon-carbon composite
materials.notes: Needs protection from air above about 450 °C; the high service temperature is in vacuum or inert gas. Expands about −1 to +2 µstrain/°C in plane (left out of the expansion axis, which is logarithmic).

materials.name: Wood-plastic composite (WPC)
materials.notes: About 50–70 % wood flour in PE, PP or PVC.

materials.name: Ethylene propylene diene rubber (EPDM)
materials.notes: Range covers unfilled to filled compounds.

materials.name: Thermoplastic vulcanisate (EPDM/PP)
materials.notes: Range covers soft to hard grades.

materials.name: Cellular glass foam
materials.notes: Closed cell, does not burn or absorb water.

materials.name: Extruded polystyrene (XPS)
materials.notes: Closed cell: takes up little water.

materials.name: Polymethacrylimide foam (PMI)
materials.notes: Withstands the heat of curing prepregs.

materials.name: Phenolic foam
materials.notes: The lowest conductivity of common insulants; resists fire well.

materials.name: High carbon steel, AISI 1080
materials.notes: Range covers annealed to quenched and tempered.

materials.name: Low alloy steel, AISI 4340
materials.notes: Range covers annealed to quenched and tempered.

materials.name: Austenitic stainless steel, 304
materials.notes: Annealed. Not magnetic in this condition.

materials.name: Austenitic stainless steel, 316
materials.notes: Annealed. Molybdenum improves resistance to chlorides.

materials.name: Grey cast iron
materials.notes: Graphite flakes give good damping and machinability but low ductility.

materials.name: Aluminium 2024-T3
materials.notes: Good fatigue resistance; poor corrosion resistance without cladding.

materials.name: Cast aluminium A356-T6
materials.notes: Sand or permanent-mould cast, heat treated.

materials.name: Copper-nickel 90/10, C70600
materials.notes: Excellent resistance to seawater and biofouling.

materials.name: Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V
materials.notes: Annealed to solution treated and aged.

materials.name: Magnesium alloy AZ31B
materials.notes: Sheet and plate. CO₂ depends strongly on the production route.

materials.name: Tungsten (commercially pure)
materials.notes: Wrought. Brittle below about 200 °C; oxidises in air above about 500 °C, so high temperatures need a protective atmosphere.

materials.name: Structural steel, EN S355
materials.notes: Hot rolled; yield strength falls slightly in thick sections.

materials.name: Case-hardening steel, AISI 8620
materials.notes: Core properties; the carburised case is far harder.

materials.name: Boron steel, 22MnB5 (press hardened)
materials.notes: Hot stamped and quenched in the die.

materials.name: High-speed steel, AISI M2
materials.notes: Hardened; strength is the bending strength.

materials.name: Austempered ductile iron, ASTM A897 Grade 1050
Abrasion-resistant white iron, ASTM A532 (Ni-Cr)
materials.notes: Very hard and brittle; cannot be machined, only ground.

materials.name: Aluminium 2219-T87
materials.notes: Welds well; keeps strength to about 200 °C.

materials.name: Aluminium 7050-T7451
materials.notes: Over-aged for resistance to stress corrosion.

materials.name: Aluminium-lithium alloy 2195-T8
materials.notes: Lighter and stiffer than other aluminium alloys.

materials.name: Cast aluminium 319-T6
materials.notes: Sand or permanent-mould cast, heat treated.

materials.name: Beryllium copper, C17200
materials.notes: Aged. Beryllium dust from machining is toxic; work it wet with extraction.

materials.name: Free-cutting brass, C36000
materials.notes: Contains lead for machining; lead-free grades exist for drinking water.

materials.name: Titanium alloy Ti-3Al-2.5V
materials.notes: Annealed to cold worked and stress relieved.

materials.name: Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo
materials.notes: Solution treated and aged; for use up to about 540 °C.

materials.name: Cast magnesium alloy AM60
materials.notes: High-pressure die cast; more ductile than AZ91.

materials.name: Magnesium alloy WE43-T6
materials.notes: Rare-earth alloy for use up to about 250 °C.

materials.name: Iron-nickel alloy 36 (low expansion)
materials.notes: Annealed. Expands very little near room temperature.

materials.name: Iron-nickel-cobalt sealing alloy, ASTM F15
materials.notes: Annealed. Expands like hard glass up to about 450 °C.

materials.name: Nickel-titanium shape-memory alloy, ASTM F2063
materials.notes: Superelastic; modulus and yield range from the martensite to the austenite state.

materials.name: Molybdenum (commercially pure)
materials.notes: Stress relieved. Oxidises in air above about 500 °C: high temperatures need vacuum or protective gas.

materials.name: Tantalum (commercially pure)
materials.notes: Annealed to cold worked. Resists almost all acids; oxidises in air above about 300 °C.

materials.name: Silver (fine)
materials.notes: Annealed to hard. The best electrical and thermal conductor.

materials.name: Beryllium (structural grade)
materials.notes: Hot isostatically pressed powder. Very stiff and light, but its dust and fume are highly toxic: work only under strict controls.

materials.name: Zirconium alloy, UNS R60804
materials.notes: Annealed. Absorbs few neutrons and resists hot water.

materials.name: Lead-free solder, Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu
materials.notes: As solidified; creeps at room temperature.

materials.name: Tungsten heavy alloy, 90 % W (W-Ni-Fe)
materials.notes: Liquid-phase sintered; machinable unlike pure tungsten.

materials.name: Oak, along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength (modulus of rupture); yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Oak, across the grain
materials.notes: Yield is the compression strength across the grain; strength is the tension strength across it.

materials.name: Pine, along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Balsa, along the grain
materials.notes: End-grain balsa is the usual core form.

materials.name: Cortical bone (human)
materials.notes: Along the long axis of the bone.

materials.name: Ash (white), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength (modulus of rupture); yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Maple (sugar), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Birch (yellow), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Douglas fir (coast), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Spruce (Sitka), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Western red cedar, along the grain
materials.notes: Naturally resists decay. Strength is the bending strength.

materials.name: Walnut (black), along the grain
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength; yield is the compression strength along the grain.

materials.name: Teak, along the grain
materials.notes: Oily and very durable outdoors. Strength is the bending strength.

materials.name: Plywood, softwood
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength along the face grain.

materials.name: Oriented strand board (OSB)
materials.notes: Strength is the bending strength along the strands.

materials.name: Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE)
materials.notes: Very high wear and impact resistance.

materials.name: Polyamide 6 (PA6, nylon 6)
materials.notes: Range covers dry to conditioned (water absorbed).

materials.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)
materials.notes: Very low friction; cannot be melt processed.

materials.name: Polyphenylene sulfide (PPS)
materials.notes: Unfilled; most grades are glass filled.

materials.name: Polylactide (PLA)
materials.notes: Made from plant sugars; industrially compostable.

materials.name: Polypropylene, impact copolymer
materials.notes: Tougher than homopolymer, especially in the cold.

materials.name: Polypropylene, 30 % glass fibre
materials.notes: Properties along the flow; short fibres.

materials.name: PVC, plasticised (flexible)
materials.notes: Range covers soft to semi-rigid compounds.

materials.name: Liquid crystal polymer (LCP), glass filled
materials.notes: Very easy flow; properties depend on direction.

materials.name: Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB, bio-based)
materials.notes: Made by bacteria; biodegrades in soil and seawater.

materials.name: PEEK, 30 % carbon fibre
materials.notes: Short fibres; properties along the flow. Conducts electricity a little.
